title: Rotating JWT signing keys with overlapping JWKS publication (sound)

input.objective: Introduce regular rotation of the JWT signing key used by the auth service; the current key has not changed in 4 years.
constraints: Access tokens live 15 minutes, refresh tokens 30 days (opaque, stored server-side).
input.context: Auth service signs access tokens (RS256) with one private key in a secrets manager; ~60 internal services validate tokens using a public key baked into their config. Services are deployed independently, some only monthly.
input.proposed_solution: Publish a JWKS endpoint with `kid`-identified public keys and move all validators to fetch it (cached for 10 minutes, refetch on unknown `kid`). Once every validator is confirmed to use JWKS (via a metric of tokens validated per method), start rotation: add the new key to JWKS, wait at least cache TTL + max token lifetime before signing with it, keep the old key published until all tokens signed with it have expired, then remove it. Automate this monthly, with alerts on unknown-kid failures.
